chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The example of the believing woman is like the example of the mole in the black bull.

key_terms.الثَّوْرِ: The bull, specifically referring to a large, strong bovine animal.
key_terms.الشَّامَةِ: A distinctive mark, mole, or spot; used here to signify rarity and uniqueness.
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُؤْمِنَةِ: The believing woman, referring to a female with strong faith and piety.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith comparing a believing woman to a mole on a black bull?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this metaphor to illustrate the scarcity of true righteousness among women, comparing a believing woman to a 'shamah' (a distinctive white mark) on a black bull. Shia scholars interpret this not as a generalization of female nature, but as a specific observation of the rarity of steadfast faith and moral excellence in the contemporary context, highlighting the exceptional status of those who possess it.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The example of the Believing woman is like the example of the mole in the black bull’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The existence of a believing woman (in rarity) is like shammah (a bright mark) on the body of a black bull.’”
